DAMGHANI:v1p218/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r9.claim: Zawj can mean a species or kind, including kinds of plants.
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r9.anchor: الثاني : الأزواج الأصناف قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r1.claim: Zawj means a type, so the phrase describes many different kinds of beneficial things sprouted from the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r2.claim: The term translated beneficial is associated with grapes, which Arabs named for their recognized benefits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r2.anchor: means “being beneficial.” The Arabs generally called grapes as

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r3.claim: Earth's abundant blessings answer those waiting for a heavenly punishment sign; God created them so people benefit and take reminders.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p403/r3.anchor: multifarious favours and blessings of God spread in the earth

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r16.claim: Since they ignored the Creator, rejected messengers, and worshiped idols, God points to His creative power and right to worship by asking them to observe the earth's growth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r16.anchor: ولما كان إعراضهم عن النظر في صانع الوجود، وتكذيب ما جاءتهم به رسله من أعظم الكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r17.claim: Zawj means a species; it may also mean a thing and its counterpart or kinds distinguished by color and taste.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r17.anchor: والزوج: النوع. وقيل: الشيء وشكله. وقيل: أبيض وأسود وأحمر وأصفر وحلو وحامض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r19.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p140/r19.claim: Mujahid and Qatada gloss karim as beautiful.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r1.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r1.claim: An unnamed gloss takes the noble plants as food eaten by people and livestock.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r2.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r2.claim: Another gloss understands noble as abundant in benefit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r3.claim: Karīm describes anything pleasing and praised, such as a beautiful face or a book valued for its meanings and benefits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r3.anchor: وقيل: الكريم صفة لكل ما يرضى ويحمد. وجه كريم: مرضي في حسنه وجماله وكتاب كريم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r4.claim: The expression also covers praiseworthy courage and strength, and essential provisions of life, including food, plants, and animals that arise from two parents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r4.anchor: وقال: حتى يشق الصفوف من كرمه، أي من كونه مرضيا في شجاعته وبأسه، ويراد الأشياء التي بها قوام الأمور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r5.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says humans come from earth's plants: those destined for Paradise are noble, while those destined for Hell are the opposite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r5.anchor: قال الشعبي: الناس من نبات الأرض، فمن صار إلى الجنة فهو كريم، ومن صار إلى النار فبضد ذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says كل gives detailed coverage of plant pairs, while كم conveys their immense number; together they signal God's complete power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r6.anchor: قلت: دل كل على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات على سبيل التفصيل، وكم على أن هذا المحيط متكاثر مفرط الكثرة، فهذا معنى الجمع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses حوله as an adverb used circumstantially, with its governing expression omitted; he explains the relation through the circumstantial phrase in 'I passed Hind laughing.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وانتصب حوله على الظرف، وهو في موضع الحال، أي كائنين حوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r2.claim: The Kufan grammarians treat الملأ as a relative expression meaning 'those who were around him,' making حوله a relative clause rather than a separately governed adverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r2.anchor: والكوفيون يجعلون الملأ موصولا، فكأنه قيل: قال للذي حوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī analyzes حوله as accusative on the surface under an implied 'settled' and locally accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: ما العامل في حوله؟ قلت: هو منصوب نصبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r4.claim: The author dismisses al-Zamakhsharī's layered parsing as needless elaboration of a basic grammatical point.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p153/r4.anchor: وهو تكثير وشقشقة كلام في أمر واضح من أوائل علم العربية

JISHUMI:v7p5342/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r3.claim: The question whether they have seen the earth's growth proves God's unity and His blessings upon creation.
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أولم يروا) على توحيده ونعمه على خلقه.

RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r3.claim: A “pair” here means a plant species; “noble” means praiseworthy in its kind, as with a beautiful face, a useful book, or a plant valued for its benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r3.anchor: والزوج هو الصنف ( من النبات ) والكريم صفة لكل ما يرضى ويحمد في بابه

RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r4.claim: One interpretation limits “noble pair” to useful plants: vegetation is beneficial or harmful, and God mentions the many useful kinds while leaving harmful ones unmentioned.
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r4.anchor: أن النبات على نوعين نافع وضار ، فذكر سبحانه كثرة ما أنبت في الأرض من جميع أصناف النبات النافع

RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation includes all plants, beneficial and harmful: God calls them all noble to signal that nothing was created without some benefit, even if people overlook it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p104#2/r5.anchor: أنه عم جميع النبات نافعه وضاره ووصفهما جميعا بالكرم

BURSEVI:v6p191#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#2/r5.claim: The interrogative hamza rebukes; the conjunction links to an omitted thought: did Quraysh reject and mock without looking at the signs?
BURSEVI:v6p191#2/r5.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار التوبيخي والواو للعطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام أي أفعل المكذبون من قريش ما فعلوا من الإعراض

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r1.claim: The earth’s marvels should deter the rejecters from their conduct and invite them to what they have turned away from.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r1.anchor: أي إلى عجائبها الزاجرة عما فعلوا الداعية إلى الإقبال إلى ما أعرضوا.

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r2.claim: God grew abundant pleasing, beneficial kinds of plants, including fragrant flowers, colorful blossoms, varied leaves, and food for people and animals.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r2.anchor: من كل صنف مرضي كثير المنافع أنبتنا فيها وتخصيص النبات النافع بالذكر

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r3.claim: Exegetes parse kam as an accusative exclamatory quantifier of abundance, with min kull zawj as its specification; kull marks comprehensiveness.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r3.anchor: قال أهل التفسير : كم خبرية منصوبة بما بعدها على المفعولية والجمع بينها وبين كل لأن كل للإحاطة بجميع أزواج النبات

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r4.claim: Kull means every kind; karīm means praiseworthy and commendable, as in a pleasing face, useful book, or brave man.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r4.anchor: والكريم من كل شيء مرضيه ومحموده يقال وجه كريم أي مرضي في حسنه وجماله وكتاب كريم مرضي في معانيه وفوائده

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r5.claim: Useful plants are singled out because they display both divine power and blessing, although even harmful plants carry wisdom and benefit.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r5.anchor: وتخصيص النبات النافع بالذكر دون ما عداه من أصناف الضار وإن كان كل نبت متضمنا لفائدة وحكمة لاختصاصه بالدلالة على القدرة والنعمة معا

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r6.claim: As the outward earth grows noble plants, God grows faith, trust, certainty, sincerity, and fine character in the hearts of gnostics.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r6.anchor: كما أنبت من أرض الظاهر كل صنف ونوع من النبات الحسن الكريم كذلك أنبت في أرض قلوب العارفين كل نبت من الإيمان والتوكل واليقين والإخلاص

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r7.claim: A Prophetic report compares the growth of faith in the heart to the growth of vegetation.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r7.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "لا إله إلا الله ينبت الإيمان كما ينبت البقل"

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r8.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r8.claim: Ibn Ṭāhir calls Adam and Eve the noblest earthly plant-pair because they occasioned the appearance of messengers, prophets, saints, and gnostics.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : أكرم زوج من نبات الأرض آدم وحواء فإنهما كانا سببا في إظهار الرسل والأنبياء والأولياء والعارفين

BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r9.speaker: الشعبي
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbī compares people to plants of the earth: those who enter Paradise are noble, and those who enter Hell are base.
BURSEVI:v6p191#3/r9.anchor: قال الشعبي : الناس من نبات الأرض فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم ومن دخل النار فهو لئيم

STUDYQURAN:26:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r1.claim: Karīm can mean good and beautiful; the verse concerns vegetation that people and animals can eat.

STUDYQURAN:26:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r2.claim: Kind can include growth that seems beneficial and growth whose benefit is not apparent; every growing thing has some benefit, though people may not know it.
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r2.anchor: notes that kind here can refer to both what is beneficial

STUDYQURAN:26:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r3.speaker: Sufyān al-Thawrī
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r3.claim: A saying attributed to Sufyān al-Thawrī calls humans growths of the earth: those entering the Garden are noble, while those entering the Fire are wretched.
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r3.anchor: Another meaning of growth appears in a saying attributed to Sufyān al-Thawrī

STUDYQURAN:26:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r4.anchor: Kind renders zawj, which also means “pair.”

STUDYQURAN:26:7/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r5.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r5.claim: Read as pair, the verse may refer to Adam and Eve, the most noble pair, ancestors of all prophets and saints.
STUDYQURAN:26:7/r5.anchor: the verse can be understood as a reference to Adam and Eve, “the most noble pair,” who gave rise to all the prophets and saints (Su).

TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r1.claim: After the earth was lifeless, God caused every beautiful kind of plant to grow; karīm means good or beautiful, as with a fruitful date palm or abundant-milk livestock.
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r1.anchor: الطيبة الحمل: كريمة، وكما يقال للشاة أو الناقة إذا غزرتا

TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the noble pairs as earth’s plants eaten by people and livestock.
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم} [الشعراء: 7] قال: من نبات الأرض، مما تأكل الناس والأنعام "

TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses “noble pair” as beautiful or good.
TAB-FULL:v17p549#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {من كل زوج كريم} [الشعراء: 7] قال: حسن "

TABATABAI:26:6-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r3.claim: The question rebukes them; its clause is conjoined to an implied reminder that they persist in turning away and have failed to look at God's plants.
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r3.anchor: الاستفهام للإنكار التوبيخي والجملة معطوف على مقدر يدل عليه المقام

TABATABAI:26:6-8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r4.claim: The verb for seeing includes the sense of looking here, which accounts for its construction with ilā.
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r4.anchor: فالرؤية في قوله { أو لم يروا } مضمنة معنى النظر ولذا عديت بإلى

TABATABAI:26:6-8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r5.claim: The apparent referent of the noble pair is a beautiful plant kind; God created plant kinds in pairs.
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالزوج الكريم. وهو الحسن

TABATABAI:26:6-8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r6.claim: Another view takes the noble pair to include animals, especially human beings, citing God's statement that He grew you from the earth like plants.
TABATABAI:26:6-8/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد بالزوج الكريم الذي أنبته الله يعم الحيوان وخاصة الإنسان

TABRISI:26:5-9/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:5-9/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:5-9/r9.claim: A pair or kind means a type together with its counterpart; karīm can mean beautiful.
TABRISI:26:5-9/r9.anchor: معناه من كل نوع معه قرينه

TABRISI:26:5-9/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:5-9/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:5-9/r10.claim: Other glosses take karīm as beneficial and praiseworthy, or as a kind prized by the people who use it.
TABRISI:26:5-9/r10.anchor: وقيل: نافع محمود مما يحتاج إليه. وقيل: من كل صنف يكرم على أهله

TABRISI:26:5-9/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:5-9/r11.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:26:5-9/r11.claim: Mujāhid says karīm refers to every kind of plant that people and livestock eat.
TABRISI:26:5-9/r11.anchor: وقيل: كريم مما يأكل الناس والأنعام عن مجاهد

TABRISI:26:5-9/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:5-9/r12.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:26:5-9/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says people are plants of the earth, citing the statement that God made humanity grow from the earth; those in Paradise are noble and those in Hell lowly.
TABRISI:26:5-9/r12.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الناس نبات الأرض كما قال سبحانه والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

TABRISI:26:5-9/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:5-9/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:5-9/r16.claim: God is al-ʿAzīz, powerful and never overcome, and al-Raḥīm, who bestows many kinds of favor on His servants.
TABRISI:26:5-9/r16.anchor: أي القادر والذي لا يعجز والغالب الذي لا يغلب { الرحيم } أي المنعم على عباده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r1.claim: Those asked to look are the people who deny the message.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r2.claim: The vegetation grows after the earth had been dead and without plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r2.anchor: بعد أن كانت ميتة لا نبات فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r3.claim: This means every kind of fruit and other fine, pleasant thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من كل صنف من أصناف الفواكه وغير ذلك حسن طيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: من كل ضرب حسن في المنظر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r5.claim: The phrase refers to plants eaten by people and livestock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p23/r6.claim: The phrase is compared with the matching expression in 22:5 and 50:7.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:7-8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:7-8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:7-8/r1.claim: A “noble kind” is every praiseworthy type of plant that people need.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:7-8/r1.anchor: من كل نوع محمود مما يحتاج إليه الناس

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says these are plants eaten by people and livestock; each kind growing from earth is a noble pair, or kind.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: نبات ما يأكل الناس والأنعام، وكل ما ينبت في الأرض فالواحد منه زوج

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r8.claim: The question is an affirmation: they have seen how many noble kinds God has grown in the earth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p495#2/r8.anchor: وهذا على الاستفهام، أي: قد رأوا كم أنبتنا في الأرض من كل زوج كريم مما رأوا.

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r4.claim: Karīm describes what is best, finest, and useful.

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r5.claim: Here zawj means a class, genus, or species.

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r6.claim: Inbāt appears to apply only to plants, but also covers animals and humans because all possess a power of growth; considering plants alone is sufficient here.
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r6.anchor: “İnbât” zâhiren nebâtâta münhasır gibi görünürse de hayvânâta ve insana dahi şâmildir.

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r7.claim: The earth displays useful plant classes with varied colors, forms, flowers, fruits, and properties, beautifully ordered within one environment.
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r7.anchor: o kadar muhtelif sınıflar, cinsler, neviler, çeşitler, o güzel çiftler nasıl tertib ve tanzim olunup çıkıyor?

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r8.claim: Plants repeatedly grow anew after drying and dying, displaying an ordered and renewing artistry.
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r8.anchor: Hem ölüp kuruduktan sonra yeniden yeniye kaç kereler bitirilip bitirilip duruyor.

ELMALILI:26:4-9/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r9.claim: Such perfect artistry cannot be the product of blind nature evolving by itself.
ELMALILI:26:4-9/r9.anchor: mükemmel sanat bir kör tabiatın kendi kendine tekâmülü eseri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r2.claim: Reason would reveal many proofs of what people deny: the life-supporting earth and the growth of varied plants and living things plainly show God's existence and power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r2.anchor: Hayata elverişli kılınmış olan yerküre ve onda her türden bitkilerin, canlıların üremesi Allah’ın varlığını ve kudretini gösteren apaçık deliller değil midir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r3.claim: Different fruits and products—with varied tastes, colors, and forms—grow on land with the same soil, water, air, and climate, proving supreme will, knowledge, wisdom, and power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r3.anchor: toprağı, suyu, havası ve iklimi aynı olan bir arazi üzerinde bitki türlerinin yaratılmasında; tadı, rengi ve şekli ayrı olan meyve ve ürünlerin meydana gelmesinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:5/r4.claim: Despite these signs, most people do not believe.

SULAMI:v2p71#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p71#4/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p71#4/r1.claim: Adam and Eve are the noblest pair to emerge from the earth and the cause through whom messengers, saints, prophets, and knowers appeared.
SULAMI:v2p71#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : أكرم زوج من نبات الأرض آدم وحواء فإنهما كانا السبب في إظهار الرسل .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r3.claim: A second sense is beauty or goodness, as in a good place, courteous speech to parents, and a beautiful plant variety.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r3.anchor: والثاني : الحسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في النساء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p316#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p316#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p316#2/r1.claim: Karīm means a beautiful or excellent kind.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p316#2/r1.anchor: {من كل زوج كريم} أي من كل جنس حسن.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r2.claim: Zawj also means kind or class: the kinds of plants, eight kinds of sheep, or every good plant species.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r2.anchor: وهو بمعنى: الصنف، قال: خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.claim: Karīm can mean good or beautiful: good plant species, beautiful growth, and gracious speech; all these senses derive from nobility.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.anchor: والكريم: الحسن، وذلك من الفضل. قال الله تعالى: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r1.claim: Kam is a multiplicative exclamatory/interrogative of abundance, governed as a direct object by the following verb; min kulli zawjin is its specification.
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r1.anchor: فهي خبرية، وهي منصوبة بما بعدها على المفعول به

SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows min kulli zawjin to be circumstantial, a parse the author says has no point.
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r2.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون حالا ولا معنى له

SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that kull gives detailed comprehensiveness over plant kinds, while kam emphasizes that this total is exceedingly numerous.
SAMIN-DURR:26:7/r3.anchor: قد دل " كل " على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات على سبيل التفصيل

ZAJJAJ:v4p83/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p83/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p83/r2.claim: Zawj means a kind, and karim means praiseworthy in its usefulness: beneficial species only the Lord of the worlds can grow and create.
ZAJJAJ:v4p83/r2.anchor: معنى زوج نوع، ومعنى كريم محمود فيما يحتاج إليه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p73#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p73#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p73#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ من كل زوج كريم ﴾ قال حسن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r1.claim: The verse turns from their rejection of revealed signs to their neglect of created signs; an omitted preceding clause reproaches their persistence in disbelief without considering earth's wonders.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r1.anchor: بيان لاعراضهم عن الآيات التكوينية بعد بيان اعراضهم عن الآيات التنزيلية والهمزة للانكار التوبيخي والواو للعطف على مقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r2.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Su'ud also supplies an omitted clause and links the verse to their turning away from signs and treating them with denial and mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو السعود بعد جعل الهمزة للانكار والعطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r3.claim: Although the link to 26:5 fits the wording, earth's wonders do not clearly disprove denial that the Qur'an came from God; this weakens that connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r3.anchor: وهو ظاهر في أن الآية مرتبطة بما قبلها من قوله تعالى ( وما يأتيهم ) الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r4.speaker: ابن كمال
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kamal supplies the sense: did they not reflect on God's wonders of power and look? The author takes this as an apparent beginning of a new discourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن كمال : التقدير ألم يتأملوا في عجئب قدرته تعالى ولم ينظروا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r5.claim: Another reading treats the verse as addressing denial of resurrection after denial of the Creator, but the author judges the first explanation clearer and preferable.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو بيان لتكذيبهم بالمعاد إثر بيان تكذيبهم بالمبدأ وكفرهم به عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r6.claim: On the preceding explanations, a genitive is omitted (wonders of the earth); alternatively, earth itself stands metonymically for its wonders.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r6.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالكلام على حذف مضاف كما أشير اليه وجوز أن يراد من الأرض عجائبها مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r7.claim: The planting clause begins a new sentence explaining the signs in the earth that should deter disbelief and call people to faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r7.anchor: استئناف مبين لما في الأرض من الآيات الزاجرة عن الكفر الداعية إلى الايمان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r8.claim: A further analysis asks readers to see how one earth was made a source for plants of many different natures; it needs neither an omitted noun nor metaphor, and the clause is a semantic بدل اشتمال.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r8.anchor: وقد يقال : المعنى أو لم ينظروا إلى نفس الأرض التي هي طبيعة واحدة كيف جعلناها منبتا لنباتات كثيرة مختلفة الطبائع

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r9.claim: خبرية كم is an object of أنبتنا and indicates abundance; كل adds comprehensive coverage, while من is either partitive or explanatory, so the particles do not repeat one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r9.anchor: وكم خبرية في موضع نصب على المفعولية بما بعدها وهي مفيدة للكثرة وجيء بكل معها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r10.claim: زوج means a kind or species; al-Raghib adds that everything in the world is paired through an opposite, likeness, or composition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r10.anchor: والزوج الصنف كما أشرنا اليه وذكر الراغب أن كل ما في العالم زوج

ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r11.claim: كريم means something commendable and praiseworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p61#2/r11.anchor: والكريم من كل شيء مرضيه ومحموده ومنه قوله :

ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r1.claim: The cited poetic line uses كريم of something praiseworthy in courage.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r1.anchor: حتى يشق الصفوف من كرمه فانه أراد من كونه مرضيا في شجاعته

ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r2.claim: كريم can restrict the kinds to those of much benefit, adding the deterrent blessing, or clarify them by teaching that God plants nothing without benefit, as 2:29 says.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r2.anchor: وهو صفة لزوج أي من كل زوج كثير المنافع وهي تحتمل التخصيص والتوضيح

ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r3.claim: Apparently the plants do not include animals; some include them because creating animals from earth counts as making them grow from it, as 71:17 indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r3.anchor: فالظاهر عدم دخول الحيوان في عموم المنبت وذهب بعض إلى دخوله بناء على أن خلقه من الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r4.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r4.claim: Al-Sha'bi explicitly includes humans: people are plants of the earth; whoever reaches Paradise is noble, while whoever reaches Hell is the opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p62/r4.anchor: وعن الشعبي التصريح بدخول الانسان فيه فقد روي عنه أنه قال الناس من نبات الأرض فمن صار إلى الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r6.claim: Zawj means a kind or variety; karīm describes good, beautiful vegetation eaten by people and livestock.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r6.anchor: صنف وضرب، {كريم} حسن من النبات مما يأكل الناس والأنعام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r7.claim: The author illustrates karīm with a date palm whose fruit is good and a she-camel that gives abundant milk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r7.anchor: يقال: نخلة كريمة إذا طاب حملها، وناقة كريمة إذا كثر لبنها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r8.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r8.claim: Al-Sha'bi likens people to plants: whoever enters Paradise is noble, and whoever enters the Fire is base.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r8.anchor: قال الشعبي: الناس من نبات الأرض فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم، ومن دخل النار فهو لئيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r5.claim: The question calls them to look at the earth’s marvels.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r6.claim: A pair is a kind or species; karīm means praiseworthy and beneficial. It may restrict kinds that indicate power or show that every plant benefits people alone or in combination.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r6.anchor: صنف. { كريم } محمود كثير المنفعة، وهو صفة لكل ما يحمد ويرضى

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:5-7/r7.claim: كل conveys the comprehensiveness of the kinds, while كم conveys their great number.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r5.claim: The earth’s signs continue the preceding call to reflect on the heavens, including their constellations and associated signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r5.anchor: وكان قد تقدم آخر تلك الحث على تدبر بروج السماء وما يتبعها من الدلالات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r6.claim: The wording turns attention toward the earth’s broad extent, varied regions, and soils; its preposition marks a limit or direction and hints at their failure to reflect.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r6.anchor: عبر للدلالة عليه بحرف الغاية فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r7.claim: God’s abundant growth in the earth follows its being barren and lifeless, displaying divine greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r7.anchor: بعد أن كانت يابسة ميتة لا نبات بها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r8.claim: Zawj here means a class or kind whose members resemble one another; God abundantly grew every kind useful to them in this life.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r8.anchor: فلم يبق صنف يليق بهم في العاجلة إلا أكثرنا من الإنبات منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r9.claim: Karīm describes what is valued and praised in its category: abundant in benefits, good in outcome, and free of impurity; the many varied plants are watered by one water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348/r9.anchor: على اختلاف ألوانها في زهورها وأنوارها

DURR-FULL:v6p289/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r4.claim: The commentary glosses every noble kind as good.
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r4.anchor: وفي قوله {كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم} قال: حسن

DURR-FULL:v6p289/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r9.claim: Mujahid explains the noble kinds as plants of the earth eaten by people and livestock.
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم} قال: من نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام

DURR-FULL:v6p289/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r10.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r10.claim: Al-Shabi says people are from the earth's growth: whoever enters Paradise is noble, and whoever enters the Fire is base.
DURR-FULL:v6p289/r10.anchor: عن الشعبي {كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم} قال: الناس من نبات الأرض فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains every noble pair as plants of the earth eaten by people and livestock.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r1.anchor: مجاهد قوله : من كل زوج كريم قال : من نبات الارص

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says people are like plants of the earth: those entering Paradise are noble, while those entering Hell are vile.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r2.anchor: الشعبي في قوله كم انبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم قال : الناس من نبات الارض

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains karīm as good or beautiful.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r3.anchor: سعيد بن جبير قوله : كريم يعني حسن

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2750#2/r4.claim: Qatada is also reported to give the same gloss of karīm as good or beautiful.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r1.claim: The clause كم أنبتنا is an appositive elaboration of يروا and carries the force of the rebuke; إلى الأرض depends on يروا.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r2.claim: كم is an exclamatory/interrogative-of-quantity expression used here as a nominal of abundance and as the object of أنبتنا: God grew many kinds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r2.anchor: أنبتنا فيها كثيرا من كل زوج كريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r3.claim: من is partitive; the abundance of كم concerns growth in many places, while كل covers the kinds and varieties of plants, together pointing to fine design.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r3.anchor: هو كثرة الإنبات في أمكنة كثيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r4.claim: The partitive phrasing makes it unnecessary to state an explicit classifier for كم, since the verse already mentions portions of each kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r4.anchor: واستغني بذكر أبعاض كل زوج عن ذكر مميز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r5.claim: زوج means a kind or species and is commonly used for types outside the animal kingdom; compare the possible reading of 13:3 and the wording of 20:53.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r5.anchor: إطلاق الزوج على النوع في غير الحيوان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r6.claim: كريم means precious or excellent within its kind; Ibn Ashur relates this usage to رزق كريم and مروا كراما.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r7.claim: The proof of God's craftsmanship also embeds a reminder of His favors: noble plants show the proof while adding the benefit of gratitude for blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r7.anchor: وهذا من إدماج الامتنان في ضمن الاستدلال لأن الاستدلال على بديع الصنع يحصل بالنظر في إنبات الكريم وغيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r8.claim: People look more readily at desirable species because they seek their benefit and admire them; the verse uses what the polytheists already pursue as a reminder that leads to proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r8.anchor: طلب المنفعة منها والإعجاب بها فإذا تطلبها وقع في الاستدلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r9.claim: That refers to the earth, God's growth of the plant kinds, and the benefits and beauty those plants contain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r9.anchor: وما في تلك الأزواج من منافع وبهجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r10.claim: إن treats the audience as if they denied that this growth and its qualities prove the oneness whose affirmation prompted their rejection of the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r10.anchor: على ثبوت الوحدانية التي هي باعث تكذيبهم الرسول لما دعاهم إلى إثباتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r11.claim: آية is singular either as a generic noun or distributively, since each of the several features mentioned constitutes a sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p101/r11.anchor: لأن في المذكور عدة أشياء في كل واحد منها آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r8.claim: Because they neglected reflection on the Creator and made idols gods, the verse directs them to God's creative power and His right to worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r8.anchor: ولما كان إعراضهم عن النظر في الصانع والإله من أعظم كفرهم وكانوا يجعلون الأصنام آلهة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r9.claim: زوج means a kind or species.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r9.anchor: و «الزوج» النوع والصنف، و «الكريم» الحسن المتقن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda gloss كريم as beautiful and well-formed or perfected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r10.anchor: و «الكريم» الحسن المتقن قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r11.claim: The phrase includes plants and foods that sustain life, and animals too because they arise from earthly growth, as 71:17 says God grew people from the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r11.anchor: ويراد الأشياء التي بها قوام الأمور والأغذية والنباتات، ويدخل في ذلك الحيوان لأنه عن إنبات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r12.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says people are plants of the earth: those who reach Paradise are noble, while those who reach the Fire are the opposite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p225#2/r12.anchor: قال الشعبي الناس من نبات الأرض فمن صار إلى الجنة فهو كريم ومن صار إلى النار فبضد ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r1.claim: The people being addressed are those who deny resurrection; they should observe how God brings forth vegetation where none had been.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r1.anchor: يعني المكذبين بالبعث كم أنبتنا فيها بعد أن لم يكن فيها نبات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses “every noble pair” as every beautiful species.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة من كل جنس حسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says zawj means a type and karīm means praiseworthy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج الزوج النوع والكريم المحمود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.claim: Zawj is a plant kind; karīm describes what is pleasing and praiseworthy in its domain. A noble face, useful book, and the poet's “from his nobility” illustrate the sense of karīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.anchor: وصف الزوج وهو الصنف من النبات بالكرم ، والكريم : صفة لكل ما يرضي ويحمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.claim: A noble plant is one whose benefits are pleasing; the poem's word karami praises the subject's bravery and valor.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.claim: The plant is pleasing in the benefits associated with it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.anchor: والنبات الكريم : المرضي فيما يتعلق به من المنافع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.claim: Kull conveys comprehensive coverage of plant kinds, while kam conveys their immense abundance; together they point to God's complete power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.anchor: قد دل { كل } على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات على سبيل التفصيل ، و { كم } على أن هذا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.claim: One explanation limits the noble kinds to useful plants and leaves harmful ones unmentioned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.anchor: يحتمل معنيين ، أحدهما : أن النبات على نوعين : نافع وضار ، فذكر كثرة ما أنبت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, all plants, useful and harmful, are included and called noble because each has some benefit and wise creation has a sound purpose.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p306#2/r8.anchor: والثاني : أن يعم جميع النبات نافعه وضاره . ويصفهما جميعا بالكرم

MUJAHID:v2p459/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p459/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p459/r1.claim: The noble pair means the kinds of plants on earth that people and livestock eat.
MUJAHID:v2p459/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ( 1 ) في قوله ﴿ من كل زوج كريم ﴾ يعني من نبات الأرض مما يأكل

MUQATIL:26:5-8/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:5-8/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:5-8/r5.claim: The earth produces many beautiful kinds and colors of plants.
MUQATIL:26:5-8/r5.anchor: كم أخرجنا من الأرض من كل صنف من ألوان النبت حسن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.claim: Kam is in the accusative as the object of anbatnā.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.claim: Zawj means a kind or species of plant.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.claim: Karīm means praiseworthy and greatly beneficial, feeding people and livestock, like a generous person whose benefit is widespread.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.anchor: محمود كثير المنفعة يأكل منه الناس والأنعام كالرجل الكريم الذى نفعه عام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.claim: Combining kam and kull signals both abundant number and comprehensive coverage of plant kinds, highlighting God's complete power.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.anchor: وفائدة الجمع بين كلمتى الكثرة والاحاطة أن كلمة كل تدل على الإحاطة بأزواج النبات

QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r7.claim: Growth on earth displays God’s greatness and power; those who looked with insight would know that only He deserves worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r7.anchor: نبه على عظمته وقدرته وأنهم لو رأوا بقلوبهم ونظروا ببصائرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses zawj as a kind or color.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r9.claim: Karīm means beautiful and noble; the root denotes honor and merit, and describes excellent, fruitful palms and virtuous, forgiving people.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r9.anchor: وأصل الكرم في اللغة الشرف والفضل

QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r10.claim: Nabata and anbata both mean to grow or cause growth; God is the one who brings forth the plants.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r11.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r11.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says people are plants of the earth: those destined for Paradise are noble and those for the Fire are lowly.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:4-9/r11.anchor: عن الشعبي أنه قال: الناس من نبات الأرض
